subject: ACME - Clarify model training / output ownership in Order Form
messages:
From: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@acme-corp.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: tim.smythe@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form — redlines attached

Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft. Please find ACME's redlines attached (ACME_MSA_Redlines_2026-05-10.docx). Our key open items are:

- Output ownership: We need unequivocal language stating ACME retains ownership of all Outputs (generated text, code, summaries) and that Redwood will not assert ownership or commercialize Outputs independent of ACME.
- Training/data use: The current "Feedback/Training" language is too broad. ACME will not permit Redwood to use Customer Data or Outputs to train or improve models unless there is an explicit, separate opt-in agreement. Aggregated telemetry MAY be acceptable if it cannot be re-associated with ACME.
- Feedback license: Any license to use customer "feedback" should be narrowly tailored (non-exclusive, limited to product improvement, exclude Outputs and PII). We also want the right to audit or request evidence that ACME data was not used to train models.

We understand Redwood's business needs but need firm protections for IP and regulated data. I've cc'd our GC Tim Smythe and we may loop in outside counsel. Would like to get to agreement on these clauses before signing the Order Form.

Can you confirm receipt and whether Redwood can provide candidate language?

Thanks,
Susan Lewis
Head of Legal Operations
ACME Corporation

Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form — proposed clause language

Hi Susan / Karthik —

Thanks for the redlines. Below is a proposed set of candidate clauses intended to reflect a compromise between ACME's concerns and Redwood's operational requirements. Please treat as negotiable starting points.

1) Definitions (proposed additions)
"Customer Data": any data, content, prompts, files, or other material that Customer uploads to or submits through the Service.
"Output": the content generated by the Service in response to Customer Data or prompts, including but not limited to text, code, images, summaries, translations, and classifications.
"Feedback": voluntary suggestions, usage metrics, anonymized telemetry, and aggregated performance data provided by Customer or collected by Redwood that are not Customer Data or Outputs.

2) Output Ownership (proposed clause)
"Customer owns all right, title and interest in and to the Outputs. Redwood hereby assigns, and to the extent any rights cannot be assigned provides Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable license to use, reproduce, display, distribute and create derivative works of the Outputs. Redwood will not assert any ownership rights in Customer Outputs or use Outputs for any purpose outside the performance of the Service except as provided in the Feedback License below."

3) Training / Use of Customer Data (proposed clause)
"Redwood will not use Customer Data or Outputs to train, improve, or further develop its foundation models or model weights, nor will it incorporate Customer Data or Outputs into any machine learning training datasets, except with Customer's prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and performance metrics that cannot reasonably be re-associated with Customer or any individual for the sole purpose of improving the Service's performance and reliability."

4) Feedback License (proposed clause)
"Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual license to use Feedback to develop, test, and enhance the Service; provided, however, that such Feedback shall not include Customer Data or Outputs. Redwood will not use Feedback in a manner that re-identifies Customer or any individual. For clarity, the Feedback license does not permit Redwood to incorporate Customer Data or Outputs into model training datasets unless Customer has given explicit written consent."

5) Audit and Compliance
"Upon reasonable written notice, Redwood will provide Customer with reasonable documentation or attestations demonstrating that Customer Data and Outputs have not been used for model training and describing the de-identification processes applied to any telemetry used for product improvements."

Rationale: These clauses allow Redwood to keep iterating on product quality via anonymized telemetry, while preserving ACME's ownership and preventing siloing of training data derived from ACME. If ACME needs a stronger audit remedy (e.g., third-party audit), we should flag cost and scope.

If ACME is comfortable with these points in principle, I can produce a redline version of the MSA and Order Form showing where the text would go. I recommend we avoid an open-ended "training" grant in the MSA and instead offer an explicit opt-in mechanism in the Order Form for any training use.

— Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[internal comment: prefer opt-in for training + narrow feedback definition]

From: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@acme-corp.com>

Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form — proposed clause language

Mina — appreciate the thoughtful draft. A few ACME counterpoints: 

- The "de-identified" carveout is too vague. We need minimum standards for de-identification (e.g., k-anonymity threshold or equivalent) and a commitment that outputs or customer prompts cannot be re-associated with ACME by Redwood or subcontractors.
- The Feedback definition must be narrower: ACME will not consider aggregated telemetry to be "Feedback" if it contains data derived from Outputs.
- We want an explicit, contractual prohibition on using Outputs for model training unless ACME signs a separate Training Addendum with specified safeguards, including the right to opt out at any time and a data handling appendix.
- Regarding audit: a right to a one-time third-party audit (at ACME's expense unless a breach is suspected) is requested.

Attached is ACME's proposed redline (ACME_proposed_language_redline.docx). We can discuss on a call — are you still available at 1:00 PM PT?

Susan
Head of Legal Operations
ACME Corporation
[attachment: ACME_proposed_language_redline.docx]

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — proposed clause language

Susan — thanks. Good points. To summarize Redwood's current posture and a suggested compromise we can present on the call: 

1) Outputs: ACME owns Outputs — Redwood will explicitly concede ownership and will not commercialize Outputs.
2) Training: Redwood will not use Customer Data or Outputs to train foundation model weights unless ACME executes a separate Training Addendum with defined safeguards and explicit consent.
3) Feedback/Telemetry: Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry (not containing Outputs or PII) to improve system performance. We propose to define de-identification standards in the security appendix (e.g., irreversible hashing + aggregation thresholds).
4) Audit: Redwood can accept a reasonable evidence obligation (e.g., attestations, logs showing data flows). For third-party audits, we need to negotiate scope and cost; Redwood cannot agree to unlimited audits without scope limits.

If that capture is accurate, we'll ask Mina to draft a narrowly-worded redline of the MSA and a short Training Addendum template ACME could sign if they choose to allow training. I've attached a brief call note stub and availability. Proposed meeting: Tue 12 May, 1:00 PM PT / 4:00 PM ET.

Best,
Karthik
